title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
authors: Yike Wang*1,2, Huaisheng Zhu*3, Zhengyu Hu2, Yige Yuan2, Zhengyu Chen3, Shakti Senthil2, Hannaneh Hajishirzi2, Yulia Tsvetkov2, Pradeep Dasigi1, Teng Xiao*1 (* equal contribution). 1 Allen Institute for AI, 2 University of Washington, 3 Independent (title block, p.1)
venue: Preprint (stated as 'Preprint.' on p.1; no venue named)
length: 13 pages, 8 body pages + 2 reference pages + 3 appendix pages. 3 tables of results (Tables 1-3), 1 configuration table (Table 4), 3 figures.
why_this_paper_was_read: [note-writer] Tasked as a possible budget-matched negative answer to ch28's question — is spending $B_s$ better than spending the same budget on $B_t$. The reading does not support that framing (see discriminant_verdict and book_impact.ch28): the budget-matched comparison exists only in the two settings where discriminant condition (1) fails, and the one setting where condition (1) holds has no test-time-scaling arm at all.

problem_stated.as_the_paper_frames_it: The paper attacks an evaluation protocol, not a mechanism. 'Existing harness evolution methods use unit test cases to search for harness configurations and then report final performance on the same public benchmark. This protocol raises two fundamental concerns.' [Abstract, p.1]
problem_stated.concern_one_missing_baseline: 'harness evolution is itself an iterative search procedure that repeatedly evaluates and revises candidate harnesses using task feedback. As in agentic test-time scaling, it should therefore be compared with simple task-level search baselines under matched feedback and inference budgets to determine whether its gains arise from improved harness design or from additional search alone.' [Abstract, p.1]
problem_stated.concern_two_shared_task_set: 'because the search and the final evaluation share the same benchmark, the reported gains risk overfitting to that specific task set.' [Abstract, p.1]. Restated as the paper's operational question: 'Does harness evolution yield generalizable improvements in harness design, or are its gains primarily due to repeated sampling?' [§1, p.2]
problem_stated.what_a_harness_is: 'A harness defines the prompts, tools, memory, verification routines, and control logic through which a model observes tasks and acts [Lopopolo, 2026].' [§1, p.2]
problem_stated.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] The problem is inherited cleanly and explicitly — from Meta-Harness [Lee et al. 2026], AHE [Lin et al. 2026] and AEVO [Zhang et al. 2026], all cited by name as the works whose protocol is faulted. But the inheritance runs entirely inside the agent-harness literature. Nothing from the sleep-time-compute corpus is inherited, cited, or visible (see cross_path_citations).

core_mechanism.one_line_unified: Harness Evolution instantiates (U-E) with the store being the agent's *operating procedure* rather than the task's content — system-prompt rules, middleware, tool guidance and long-term memory — written offline by a meta agent from an accumulated evidence store and, in the unit-test setting, selected by a real verifier; Theta and W never move. The paper's three other methods are foils: Parallel Sampling and Sequential Refinement are pure wake-time scaling ($B_s=0$), and Harness Scaling applies the same write operator on the wrong clock.

notation_conflicts.preamble: The paper numbers only two equations (the pass@1 and pass@k definitions in App. A.5). All method equations in §3 are unnumbered display lines, so every 'original equation' locator below is a section locator. Reserved-symbol collisions are unusually dense because the paper is an RL/agent-evaluation paper and the monograph's reserved set is a memory/training set.

equations_unified.latex: E_1 \;=\; h_1 \;=\; \{\text{one bash tool}\}, \qquad \text{no skills, no middleware, no persistent memory}
equations_unified.gloss: The initial state of the store, and it is deliberately minimal. Every one of the four methods starts here, so the same artifact is both the frozen harness of the two test-time-scaling arms and the seed of the two harness arms.
equations_unified.source: [App. A.1, p.11: 'All four methods initialize the code agent from an identical minimal harness: the model is granted access to a single bash tool and nothing else, without skills, middleware, or persistent memory.'] + [§4.1, p.5]

equations_unified.gloss: Retrieval is the identity, exactly as in Letta STC: the whole harness is in force on every request. There is no index, no scoring, no selection. Unlike Letta STC the store is not spliced only into the prompt — part of it is middleware and tool wiring that executes.

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{sleep write (U-E), Harness Evolution:}\qquad E_k \;=\; \mathrm{wr}\big(E_{k-1},\ \hat c_k\big) \;=\; \hat c_k, \qquad \hat c_k \;=\; S\big(\mathcal{H}_{k-1};\ B_s/(K-1)\big), \qquad k=2,\ldots,K,\ \ K=5
equations_unified.gloss: wr is FULL REPLACEMENT — the meta agent emits the next harness, not a patch. This is Letta STC's destructive overwrite again, on a different payload.

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{evidence accumulation (pure union):}\qquad \mathcal{H}_k \;=\; \mathcal{H}_{k-1}\cup\{e_k\}, \qquad e_k \;=\; \big(E_k,\ \{\hat y_k^{(i,j)}\}_{i,j}\big) \ \text{or}\ \big(E_k,\ \{\hat y_k^{(i,j)}\}_{i,j},\ \{R(\hat y_k^{(i,j)},g^{(i)})\}_{i,j}\big)
equations_unified.gloss: TWO write operators coexist, as in Letta STC and ReasoningBank: the artifact $E$ is overwritten, the evidence log $\mathcal{H}$ is a pure union with no eviction, no decay, no compaction. The paper never remarks on the difference. $\mathcal{H}$ is read only by the meta agent; only $E$ is read at wake.

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{write verification:}\qquad \hat E \;=\; \begin{cases} E_K & \text{no unit tests}\\[2pt] \arg\max_{k\le K}\ \bar R(E_k),\quad \bar R(E_k)=\dfrac{1}{n_{\text{search}}m}\sum_{i}\sum_{j} R\big(\hat y_k^{(i,j)},g^{(i)}\big) & \text{unit tests available}\end{cases}
equations_unified.gloss: This is the strongest write verification in the corpus. Letta STC verifies $\hat c$ not at all; ReasoningBank verifies with an LLM judge that is 72.7% accurate; here the selector is a real unit test executed in a sandbox. The finding of §4.4 is therefore not 'the write was unverified' — the write was verified, and still did not transfer.

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{held-out application (§4.4 — the only discriminant-passing configuration):}\qquad \hat y \;\sim\; f\big(q;\ \Theta,\ W,\ \hat E\big), \qquad q \in \mathcal{D}_{\text{test}},\ |\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}|=34, \qquad N_q = 34
equations_unified.gloss: One artifact, evolved on 45 training tasks and selected on 10 validation tasks, serves 34 tasks it has never seen. This is the amortisation identity (A) with the largest and cleanest $N_q$ anywhere in the corpus — and the artifact buys +0.6 points on average.

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{Harness Scaling — same operator, wake clock:}\qquad E_k \;=\; \mathrm{wr}\big(E_{k-1},\ S(q,\,E_{k-1},\,\hat y_{k-1};\ B_t)\big), \qquad \hat y = \hat y_K,\qquad E \text{ discarded}
equations_unified.gloss: The update conditions on the evaluation task $q$ itself, so the query has already arrived; and the artifact dies with the instance, so nothing is carried to a later query. Two of the four discriminant conditions fail. The paper's own words: 'harness scaling adapts the harness for a single evaluation instance by allocating additional inference budget to harness revision... instance-guided harness adaptation, in contrast to dataset-guided harness evolution.' This is the cleanest foil in the corpus for condition (1).

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{test-time arms:}\quad \text{Parallel: } \hat y=\arg\max_{k\le K} J_{\text{self}}(\hat y_k) \ \text{ or }\ \hat y\in\{\hat y_k: R(\hat y_k,g)=1\}; \qquad \text{Sequential: } \hat y_k\sim f\big(q,\,S(\hat y_{k-1};B_t);\ \Theta,W,E\big),\ E\ \text{fixed}
equations_unified.gloss: $B_s = 0$ for both. Note that Sequential Refinement does pay for the summariser $S$ at wake, and Parallel Sampling pays for a self-judge; neither pays for a meta agent.

Stated as the defining premise of the whole harness literature, not derived. 'Test-time scaling refers to improving a language model's outputs by allocating additional computation at inference, without modifying the model weights'; 'A growing body of work improves agent performance without retraining the underlying model by optimizing the external scaffold around the model.'

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{the budget identity the paper actually enforces:}\qquad K \;=\; 5 \ \text{rollouts per task, all four arms}, \qquad m=1
equations_unified.paper_form: 'we sample one rollout per task for each harness, setting m = 1, to match the rollout budget across methods. We use a compute budget of K = 5 across methods.'
equations_unified.gloss: CRITICAL READING. The matched quantity is a count of agent rollouts, not tokens and not FLOPs. Table 4 caps a single rollout at 300 model turns x 128,000 generated tokens, so a rollout is not a unit of compute. And the two harness arms additionally run a meta agent capped at 500 model turns — a HIGHER cap than the code agent's 300 — plus an Agent Debugger at 25 turns, neither of which the parallel-sampling arm pays. In the monograph's units the arms are $B_s=0,\ B_t=Kb_{\text{roll}}+b_J$ (Parallel); $B_s=0,\ B_t=Kb_{\text{roll}}+(K-1)b_S$ (Sequential); $B_s=Kn_{\text{search}}b_{\text{roll}}+(K-1)(b_S+b_M),\ B_t=b_{\text{roll}}$ (Harness Evolution); $B_s=0,\ B_t=Kb_{\text{roll}}+(K-1)(b_S+b_M)$ (Harness Scaling). None of $b_{\text{roll}}, b_S, b_M, b_J$ is measured.

what_is_NOT_in_the_mechanism: No weight update of any kind. No gradient, no optimizer, no adapter, no LoRA, no fine-tuning. Stated as the premise of the literature, not as a limitation. [§2, p.2]

No fast-weight or activation-space state. The KV cache is never mentioned; 'Max context 200,000 tokens' and a 'Context compaction threshold 0.75' are the only nods at context management and they appear only in the configuration table. [Table 4, p.12]
No retrieval. $\mathrm{ret}$ is the identity — the whole harness is in force on every request. There is no index, no embedding, no top-$m$, no scoring over stored items.

No eviction, expiry, compaction or capacity bound on either $E$ or $\mathcal{H}$. The only stated consequence of unbounded growth is a qualitative one: 'the growing volume of persistent prompt text introduces context bloat that can offset the remaining gains'. [§5.1, p.8]
No budget sweep. $K=5$ is the single operating point for every method in every table.

No cost measurement of any kind. Zero tokens consumed, zero FLOPs, zero wall-clock, zero dollars, zero GPU-hours. A whole-text probe returns 'FLOP' 0 times and the word 'cost' exactly once, at [§3.1, p.3], where it names something the summariser might report.

outer_vs_inner.headline: The outer-loop column is empty, as in Letta STC — nothing is trained. But the moving-part column is richer: three separate frozen-model agents (code agent, Agent Debugger, meta agent) run at three different points in the loop, and only one of them is on the wake path.

outer_vs_inner.reader_takeaway: [note-writer] For the monograph this is the cleanest existing separation of *what is frozen and what evolves* in an agent stack, and Figure 2 (p.3) draws it explicitly with a 'Frozen / Evolving' legend. It is the first paper in this corpus where the offline write is performed by a distinct agent with its own budget, and that fact is what breaks the budget matching (see H10).

update_layer.instantiates: (U-E) — and only (U-E). No layer other than $E$ moves anywhere in the paper.
how_this_paper_differs_from_the_canonica: The content of $E$ is PROCEDURAL, not propositional. Every other $E$-path paper in the corpus stores something about the task's content — RAG chunks, Mem0 facts, Zep graph entities, ReasoningBank strategies, Letta STC's re-represented context. Here the store holds the agent's operating procedure: behavioural rules, middleware code, tool guidance, and a long-term memory block. This is a new sub-kind of $E$ and it should be entered in the concept ledger.

The store's SCOPE is the task distribution, not a context. Letta STC's store is scoped to one context and dies with it; Mem0's and Zep's are scoped to a user or a session. Harness Evolution's artifact is a single per-deployment object that serves every task. In (A) this makes $N_q$ the size of the served task set — 34 in §4.4 — rather than a per-context handful.

The write is VERIFIED by a real verifier when unit tests are available: $\hat E$ is the harness with the highest measured aggregate outcome $\bar R$ over the search batch [§3.4, p.4]. This is stronger write hygiene than anything else in the corpus, and it changes what a negative result means — the failure is not a bad write, it is a write that was measured to be good on the search set and did not transfer.

The number of rounds is EXPLICIT and small: $K=5$, so $k$ ranges over exactly five sleep rounds, and the paper states it. Letta STC ran exactly one round; ReasoningBank runs one per task; this is one of the few corpus papers with a stated multi-round offline loop. It is still not a sweep — $K$ is never varied.

$\mathrm{wr}$ is DESTRUCTIVE OVERWRITE of the artifact ($M$ emits the next harness whole) while $\mathcal{H}$ is PURE UNION. The paper uses two write operators without naming the difference — the same unremarked doubling that letta-stc and reasoningbank exhibit.

other_layers.U-W: not touched — no fast-weight state exists in the systems used
other_layers.U-Theta: not touched, and excluded by the literature's premise: 'improves agent performance without retraining the underlying model' [§2, p.2]. The paper does not gesture at a Theta-path composition even as future work.

update_layer.ordering: Single-layer. For Harness Evolution: $K-1$ offline (U-E) writes over a task batch, then one wake read per held-out query. For Harness Scaling: $K-1$ (U-E) writes interleaved with wake reads on the SAME query, then discard.

B_s.detail: No token count, FLOP count, wall-clock figure, dollar figure or GPU-hour appears anywhere in the paper. Whole-text probe: 'FLOP' occurs 0 times; the word 'cost' occurs exactly once and it is at [§3.1, p.3] naming something the summariser may report, not a measurement. What IS reported is (i) a rollout count, $K=5$ per task for every method with $m=1$ rollout per task per round [§4.1, p.5], and (ii) per-agent CAPS in the configuration table — code agent 300 model turns, Agent Debugger 25 turns, meta agent 500 turns, all with 200,000 max context and 128,000 max generation per turn [Table 4, p.12]. Caps are not consumption.
B_s.finding: This is a paper whose entire contribution is a budget-matched comparison, and it reports the budget as a count of agent rollouts. A rollout is bounded above by 300 turns x 128k generated tokens, so it is a unit of work, not a unit of compute. ch28's six-bin taxonomy has no bin for this form (see book_impact.ch28).

L_w.detail: Zero latency, TTFT, ms/token, wall-clock or throughput numbers. A whole-text probe for latency / wall-clock / seconds / dollars returns nothing. The wake-side cost delta of the method is acknowledged in prose and never quantified: 'the growing volume of persistent prompt text introduces context bloat that can offset the remaining gains' [§5.1, p.8]. The evolved harness rides in the system prompt on every request, so this is a real per-query prefill increase with no number attached.
L_w.proxy_values_actually_reported: None. Unlike Letta STC, which at least prints a generated-token axis, this paper reports no compute proxy at all — only accuracy.

C.detail: No byte, character or token count for the evolved harness at any round. The composition is described (system-prompt rules, long-term memory, middleware such as turn-budget trackers and output truncation and finalization gates, tool guidance) [§5.1, pp.7-8] and the initial state is described exactly ('a single bash tool and nothing else, without skills, middleware, or persistent memory') [App. A.1, p.11], but the artifact is never sized. The 200,000-token max context [Table 4, p.12] is an upper bound on everything in the prompt, not a measurement of $E$.
C.finding: This is the corpus's first $E$-path artifact whose capacity is O(1) in users — one harness per deployment rather than one per user or per session — and it is still unsized. ch26's count of papers printing $C_{\text{cap}}$ is unchanged.

rho.value: absent as a rate; the SIGN is observable and negative under self-feedback
rho.detail: No per-round curve is printed anywhere, so no degradation rate can be computed. But the endpoints of a 5-round offline loop are printed and they go the wrong way when the feedback is the agent's own judgement: Harness Evolution ends below the initial harness on the three-model average (67.4 vs 68.2) and 5.6 points below on GPT-5.4 (69.7 vs 75.3) [Table 1, p.6]. The paper reads this as compounding: 'Self generated feedback is noisy, and sequential revision based on such feedback risks compounding early mistakes' [§4.2, p.6]. With unit-test feedback the sign flips positive (75.8 vs 72.9 on pass@1) [Table 2, p.6]. The qualitative degradation mechanism is named — context bloat from monotonically growing prompt text [§5.1, p.8] — and never measured.
rho.finding: The corpus's usual complaint is that $\rho$ is out of scope by construction (Letta STC ran one round). Here five rounds are run and the endpoint moves, so $\rho$ is in scope and simply unreported. That is a different and more culpable kind of absence.

N_q.value: structurally explicit in one setting; never a deployment distribution
N_q.detail: In §4.4 one artifact serves 34 held-out tasks, so $N_q=34$ — the largest and cleanest amortisation denominator in the corpus, and the first one that is a property of the design rather than a synthetic sweep. In §4.2/§4.3 the artifact serves the same 89 tasks it was searched on, so $N_q$ is not well defined (the artifact has seen the query). No real workload distribution is reported, so ch25 §25.3.3's count of papers reporting a serving $N_q$ distribution is unchanged.
N_q.finding: [note-writer] This is the point ch25 and ch28 should take. The amortisation arithmetic here is maximally favourable — a large $N_q$, a shared prefix, a one-time offline cost — and the method still fails. For this artifact class the binding constraint is not the cost denominator; it is whether the artifact carries anything transferable.

experiments.result_tables_exist: Three result tables with printed numbers (Tables 1-3), plus a configuration table (Table 4). This is a genuine strength relative to the corpus: unlike Letta STC, every headline number in this paper can be read off a table rather than a line plot. No error bars, confidence intervals, standard deviations or seeds are reported anywhere.

table_1_no_unit_tests_pass_at_1.authors_reading: 'Parallel Sampling is the most consistent approach, improving the average score from 68.2 to 72.3 and yielding gains on all three models. In contrast, Harness Evolution fails to outperform the direct sampling baseline on average. unfavorable_facts.fact: The only experiment that isolates the reusable artifact has no test-time-scaling arm. Table 3 compares Harness Evolution against direct sampling at $K=1$ and nothing else.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'The other three methods are not directly applicable in this setting, since they rely on instance-level scaling or refinement rather than producing a reusable artifact.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The paper's headline claim is that harness evolution does not beat simple test-time scaling under matched budgets. That comparison is run only in §4.2 and §4.3, where the harness was searched on the very tasks it is scored on — the protocol the paper itself indicts. In §4.4, where the search and evaluation sets are disjoint, the matched-budget comparison is dropped. The clean protocol and the matched-budget comparison never co-occur in this paper.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Budgets are matched in ROLLOUTS, not in computation, and the residual runs against the harness arms.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'we sample one rollout per task for each harness, setting m = 1, to match the rollout budget across methods. We use a compute budget of K = 5 across methods.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: A rollout is not a unit of compute: Table 4 caps one at 300 model turns x 128,000 generated tokens. The two harness arms additionally invoke a meta agent capped at 500 model turns — a HIGHER cap than the code agent's 300 — and an Agent Debugger at 25 turns, neither of which Parallel Sampling pays. No token, FLOP, wall-clock or dollar figure appears anywhere in the paper ('FLOP': 0 occurrences; 'cost': 1 occurrence, not a measurement). So the phrase 'under a unified budget' names a rollout identity that cannot be audited as a compute identity. The direction is conservative for the paper's conclusion — harness evolution loses while spending uncounted extra compute — and fatal for any use of this paper as a budget-matched datum in the monograph's accounting.

unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The paper's claim is about how a budget should be ALLOCATED, and it never varies the budget. Harness Evolution is the arm whose cost is amortised over the whole task distribution, so it is the arm most plausibly starved at $K=5$ — five rounds, one rollout per task, over a 45-task search set — and any crossover at larger $K$ is untestable from this paper. In ch28's terms the paper places one point on the $B_s$ axis and reads a ranking off it.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The authors supply two explanations that make the negative result benchmark-conditional, and the abstract does not carry the condition.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'agents already achieve relatively high scores on Terminal-Bench, and the small set of remaining failures may stem from limitations in the underlying model rather than deficiencies in the harness'; 'Terminal-Bench may simply not be very sensitive to harness design: a minimal setup consisting of a shell tool and a basic prompt already suffices for most solvable tasks'; 'the value of automatic harness evolution is likely task dependent'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The abstract states 'automatic harness evolution does not consistently outperform simple test-time scaling methods and exhibits limited generalization' without the benchmark condition that §5.2 concedes. A reader who stops at the abstract acquires a general negative result the paper does not claim.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Two runs, no dispersion, and differences the paper interprets are a few task-flips wide.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: On the 89-task suite at one rollout per task one task is 1.12 pass@1 points. Table 1's key interpreted differences are $-0.8$ (Harness Evolution vs initial harness, average), $+1.1$ (Sequential Refinement's 'marginal average improvement'), and $-2.3$ (Sequential Refinement's 'slightly degrades GPT-5.4'). None is accompanied by a dispersion statistic, and the two-run averaging that was performed is never reported as a spread.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Harness Scaling is presented under the 'Automatic Harness Evolution' heading in both Figure 1 and Table 1, yet it has no offline phase at all.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: Its update conditions on the evaluation task itself, $h_k = M(x,\Phi(h_{k-1},y_{k-1}))$ [§3.5, p.5], and its artifact is discarded after the instance. It is test-time scaling in harness space. Grouping it with Harness Evolution in the headline figure lets a reader draw a conclusion about offline harness design from the arm that does none — and it is the arm with the best single result in Table 1 (76.0 on Claude) and the best harness-side average (71.8).

unfavorable_facts.fact: The same model instance writes the harness, summarises the traces, and solves the tasks — with no cross-model control.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: 'a summarization map $\Phi$, realized by the same underlying model as the policy' [§3.1, p.3], and Table 4 lists the same model row for the code agent, the Agent Debugger and the meta agent. Whether a harness written by model A helps model B — the most natural test of whether an artifact encodes reusable design rather than model-specific habit — is never run, although two frontier models were available in every setting.

unfavorable_facts.fact: One of the six case studies shows the write flipping back to failure and the caption does not remark on it.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'count-dataset-tokens: fail -> pass at iter 2 ... 4 + result: FAIL -> PASS (iteration 2, 4, 5)'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The result line enumerates iterations 2, 4 and 5 as passes, which means iteration 3 regressed after two accepted edits. This is a within-search $\rho$ signal of exactly the kind the corpus keeps failing to find, and it is printed in a figure whose header says 'fail -> pass at iter 2'.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Zero cost, latency, capacity or throughput measurement of any kind, in a paper about spending compute well.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: All four of the monograph's cost cells are empty. There is no token count of any arm's consumption, no wall-clock, no dollars, no GPU-hours, no bytes for the artifact. The word 'cost' appears once in the whole paper and names something the summariser might mention [§3.1, p.3]. The appendix even records a token-consumption motive for the Agent Debugger's file-based interface — 'which reduces token consumption while preserving access to full detail when needed' [App. A.2, p.11] — so token accounting was a design concern and never a measurement.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The 45/10/34 split rule is not stated, and the split is the load-bearing construct of the paper's central claim.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: §4.4 says only 'we split Terminal-Bench 2.1 into 45 training tasks, 10 validation tasks, and 34 held-out test tasks'. Whether the split is random, stratified by difficulty, or stratified by task family is not said, and Terminal-Bench tasks are heterogeneous (the case studies range from Caffe builds to SQLite WAL repair to MTEB retrieval). A split that puts the harness-sensitive tasks on one side would move the result. No seed and no repetition of the split is reported.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Held-out here means held-out within one benchmark, not held-out across benchmarks.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'evaluate whether evolved harnesses transfer to held-out tasks from the same benchmark'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: The paper's own §2 states the scope precisely, but §4.4's conclusion — 'current harness evolution algorithms exhibit limited generalization ability' — is stated without it. The stronger and more relevant transfer question, whether a harness evolved on one benchmark helps on another, is never posed.

The paper reinvents the offline-versus-wake budget question inside the agent-harness community without touching a single paper that has been asking it.

E_path.finding: A 2026 $E$-path artifact paper that stores procedural experience for reuse across tasks cites none of the memory line that has been doing the same thing since 2023. Its nearest neighbour in the corpus is ReasoningBank — same shape, same reuse claim, same degradation-with-growth observation — and neither paper knows the other exists.

W_path.citations: ZERO. No test-time training, no fast weights, no Titans/Atlas/TTT line, no linear attention, no state-space models, no recurrent memory. The KV cache is never mentioned; 'Max context' and 'Context compaction threshold' appear only as configuration rows [Table 4, p.12].

Theta_path.citations: ZERO, and excluded by premise rather than by oversight: 'improves agent performance without retraining the underlying model by optimizing the external scaffold around the model' [§2, p.2]. No LoRA, no PEFT, no model editing, no continual learning, no distillation. Unlike Letta STC, the paper does not even name the $\Theta$-path as future work.

bio_CLS_path.finding: The word 'sleep' occurs exactly three times in the whole paper and every occurrence is the Unix `sleep(1)` command inside a shell trace: 'repeated sleep/check turns', 'short shell timeout and sleep polling consumed build budget', 'smart wait loop replaces repeated sleep commands' [App. B, Figure 3, p.13]. The corpus's central term survives in this paper only as a shell builtin. That is the sharpest available illustration of the monograph's thesis that the NAME travelled and the mechanism did not.

cross_path_citations.shared_ancestry_with_letta_stc: Two entries in common — Snell et al. 2024 and Brown et al. 2024, both test-time-scaling papers. Both this paper and Letta STC root themselves in the test-time-scaling literature rather than in memory research, and both define their contribution by contrast with it. Letta STC added caching and speculative decoding as its systems ancestry; this paper adds prompt/program optimisation (DSPy, MIPRO, GEPA, TextGrad) and evolutionary search (AlphaEvolve). Neither reaches the other.
cross_path_citations.monograph_implication: [note-writer] The silence map of the dossier gains a row that runs in a new direction. The earlier finding was that the $W$- and $\Theta$-path papers inherited the phrase 'sleep-time compute' from a paper that never cited them. Here a fourth community — agent harness engineering — independently arrives at the same question (is offline artifact-building worth its budget relative to spending the budget at wake?), builds a better protocol for answering it than anything in the corpus, and cites nobody. The cost of the silence is concrete and measurable this time: this paper's §4.4 needed exactly one more table to answer the corpus's open question, and nothing in its bibliography would have told it that the question was open.

systems_implications.preamble: Grounding key: [PAPER] = a statement or number on the page with a locator; [INFERENCE] = the note-writer's translation, not in the paper. This paper supplies zero systems numbers, so almost everything below is [INFERENCE] built on stated mechanism.

items.claim: The mechanism is prompt and scaffold substitution. Nothing in the serving stack changes; $\Theta$ is frozen, so shared-weight batching is preserved exactly as in the rest of the $E$-path.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §2, p.2 ('without retraining the underlying model', 'without modifying the model weights'). [INFERENCE] for the batching consequence.

items.claim: The artifact is a per-DEPLOYMENT object, not per-user or per-session. One harness serves the whole task distribution. Its storage cost is therefore O(1) in users — the cheapest capacity profile any path in the corpus can offer.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §3.4, p.4 ('optimize across a task distribution rather than fitting to one task'); §4.4, p.7 (one $\hat E$ evaluated on 34 held-out tasks). [INFERENCE] for the capacity consequence. The bytes are never reported, so the profile is structural only.

items.claim: At wake the artifact is a SHARED PREFIX across every request in the deployment, so prefix caching applies maximally — the most favourable prefill situation an $E$-path artifact can have.
items.grounding: [INFERENCE], grounded in H2 and in the artifact's per-deployment scope. The paper measures neither the cost nor the saving; it has no cost model at all. Contrast Letta STC, whose $\hat c$ is shared only across the $N_q$ queries of one context.

items.claim: The wake-side cost nevertheless RISES and is unbounded on the page: the evolved harness accumulates prompt text monotonically across rounds and rides in the system prompt on every request.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §5.1, p.8: 'the growing volume of persistent prompt text introduces context bloat that can offset the remaining gains'. [INFERENCE] for the per-request prefill consequence. No harness length is printed at any round, so the delta cannot be computed. Same structural gap as Letta STC's unmeasured $|\hat c|$.

items.claim: The sleep-side work is a textbook batch-tier job: a meta agent and a summarisation agent, both latency-insensitive, both off the request path, both capped at large turn budgets. This is exactly the interactive-tier-to-batch-tier conversion Letta STC priced at 10:1 — and this paper prices it at nothing.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §3.4, p.4 for the offline loop; Table 4, p.12 for meta agent 500 turns / debugger 25 turns / 128,000 generation per turn / 200,000 context. [INFERENCE] for the tiering reading.

items.claim: Sleep wall-clock is bounded by a SEQUENTIAL chain, not by parallel width: $K-1$ meta-agent invocations, each reading the accumulated store and each preceded by $n_{\text{search}}$ rollouts that must complete first. At $K=5$, $n_{\text{search}}=45$, $m=1$ that is 4 sequential barriers over 225 rollouts.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §3.4, p.4; §4.1, p.5; §4.4, p.7. [INFERENCE] for the barrier structure and the arithmetic. The paper reports no wall-clock, so pre-warm throughput cannot be estimated.

items.claim: The sleep budget here includes ENVIRONMENT provisioning, not just tokens. 'Each rollout executes in its own freshly provisioned E2B remote sandbox.'
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. A.4, p.11. [INFERENCE] for the accounting consequence: no paper in the corpus has a cost cell that can hold sandbox provisioning, and for agentic $E$-path writes it may dominate token cost. This is a genuine gap in the monograph's four-cell cost frame, which assumes the sleep budget is model compute.

items.claim: The pass@1-to-pass@5 gap is a directly useful serving number and the paper names what it means. With unit tests, Sequential Refinement's gap is 91.8 − 84.3 = 7.5 points and Harness Evolution's is 86.2 − 75.8 = 10.4 points.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Table 2, p.6; App. A.5, p.11: 'the gap between the two reflects the variance of the agent across independent attempts'. [INFERENCE] For a serving stack that gap is the value of retry-with-verifier, a pure wake-time knob that needs no offline state and no persistent store at all — which is the paper's own conclusion restated in serving terms.

items.claim: Where the traffic lands: a per-deployment configuration blob (system prompt text, middleware code, tool descriptions) → tokenizer → prefill → KV cache, plus a middleware execution path. Never HBM-resident weights, never optimizer state, never a per-user shard.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §1, p.2 for the harness composition; §5.1, pp.7-8 for the middleware layer. [INFERENCE] for the hierarchy walk. Note the one novelty against the rest of the $E$-path: part of this store is not text in a prompt but CODE in the control loop, so a fraction of the artifact never touches the model at all.

items.claim: The standing reader question — what changes at decode — has the same answer as every other $E$-path paper, and the same limit. Nothing about the decode kernel changes; only the prompt and the control loop change. Capacity cannot be raised the way the $\Theta$-path raises it.

discriminant_verdict.the_test: PRE-RESEARCH §2.1: (1) before the query arrives, (2) spending $B_s>0$, (3) actually changing the state of one of $\Theta$/$W$/$E$, (4) with that change used by LATER queries. All four required.
discriminant_verdict.headline: The paper contains four methods and they land in three different places. Harness Evolution PASSES all four conditions in the §4.4 protocol and FAILS condition (1) in the §4.2/§4.3 protocol — same algorithm, same write operator, same budget, different task split. Harness Scaling FAILS (1) and (4). Parallel Sampling and Sequential Refinement FAIL (1), (2) and (3). The paper cannot be given a single verdict.

discriminant_verdict.which_condition_decides: **Condition (1), decisively and twice.** Conditions (2) and (3) are never in doubt anywhere in the paper — the harness is unambiguously external state, $\Theta$ never moves, and a budget is unambiguously spent. Condition (4) is the second cut and it removes Harness Scaling even under a lenient reading of (1). But condition (1) is what separates the same algorithm from itself across two protocols, and it is what separates Harness Evolution from Harness Scaling. Nothing else in this paper does any classification work.
discriminant_verdict.the_second_justification_for_condition_1: ch11 §11.2.3 justifies condition (1) MECHANISTICALLY — without it, a write inside the user turn is indistinguishable from a sleep write and 'sleep-time compute' becomes another name for 'writing'. This paper supplies an independent EVIDENTIAL justification for the same cut, arrived at with no knowledge of the monograph's frame: when the search tasks and the evaluation tasks coincide, the reported gain is not attributable to the artifact, because the artifact may encode the answers. Two unrelated arguments select the same condition. That is the strongest external corroboration condition (1) has received.
discriminant_verdict.second_instance_of_setting_dependent_pas: ch27's evidence item B4 already records that `Do LMs Need Sleep?` passes the discriminant only in the Depo setting. This is the second instance, in a different path, and it is sharper: there the two settings differ in dataset layout (whether the question precedes the context), here the mechanism, the write operator, the budget and the model are byte-identical across the two protocols and only the train/test split moves. The consequence for the frame is stated plainly — the discriminant applies to (mechanism, protocol) pairs, not to papers, and a per-paper census cannot represent this paper at all.
discriminant_verdict.counting_rule_recommendation: [note-writer] If this paper ever enters a census, it must enter as ONE passing configuration (Harness Evolution under the §4.4 protocol) plus ONE explicit foil (Harness Scaling) plus TWO non-candidates, not as one paper with one label. The dossier's counting convention — pass 9 / borderline 1 / fail 19 over 29 papers — has no cell for a paper whose verdict depends on which of its own experiments is being asked about.

book_impact.summary_one_line: The paper CONFIRMS ch28's verdicts 1 and 6, ch27's verdicts 2 and 5, and ch11/ch24's condition (1); it THREATENS nothing outright; it QUALIFIES ch28 verdict 5's optimism about the cost of fixing the literature; and it does NOT deliver the budget-matched answer the tasking premise expected, because the matched comparison and the clean protocol never co-occur in it.

correction_to_the_tasking_premise.the_premise: That this paper is a budget-matched negative answer to ch28's question — is spending $B_s$ better than spending the same budget on $B_t$ — and that ch28's verdict therefore changes.
correction_to_the_tasking_premise.why_it_does_not_hold: Two independent reasons. (i) The matched-budget comparison exists only in §4.2 and §4.3, and in both of those the harness was searched on the very tasks it is scored on, so discriminant condition (1) fails and the arm being compared is not sleep-time compute. (ii) In §4.4, the only configuration where condition (1) holds, the test-time-scaling arms are absent by the authors' own decision: 'The other three methods are not directly applicable in this setting, since they rely on instance-level scaling or refinement rather than producing a reusable artifact' [§4.4, p.7]. So a discriminant-passing $E$-path procedure is never compared against a matched-budget wake-time arm anywhere in this paper.
correction_to_the_tasking_premise.and_the_budget_was_not_matched_in_a_comp: Even in §4.2/§4.3 the matching is $K=5$ ROLLOUTS, not tokens or FLOPs [§4.1, p.5]. A rollout is capped at 300 model turns x 128,000 generated tokens, and the harness arms additionally run a meta agent capped at 500 turns and a debugger at 25 turns [Table 4, p.12], none of it counted. The residual runs against harness evolution, so the negative finding is conservative — but 'matched budget' does not survive translation into the monograph's units.
correction_to_the_tasking_premise.what_the_paper_actually_delivers: The best-designed protocol in this corpus for the question, executed such that its two halves never meet. It is one table away from answering ch28's question, and that missing table is now the sharpest falsifier the monograph can name.

verdict_1.relation: CONFIRMS, and does not trigger any falsifier
verdict_1.detail: ch28 판정 1 — '현재 문헌으로 $B_s$–품질 곡선은 그릴 수 없다' — survives untouched. Against ch28's minimum reporting requirements this paper satisfies R4 strongly (one public benchmark, one metric, a common initial harness, all arms on the same footing — the first paper in view to do this) and R9 (numbers in tables, not read off plots); it partially satisfies R2 (Table 4 prints caps, never consumption, and no MFU or throughput), R5 (the amortisation scope is explicit — one artifact per task distribution, $N_q=34$ in §4.4 — but no deployment distribution) and R8 ($K=5$ stated, never varied); and it FAILS R1 (no absolute FLOPs or tokens; 'FLOP' occurs 0 times), R3 (a single budget point, no sweep), R6 (context bloat asserted, never counted) and R7 (no $C_{\text{cap}}$ of any kind). ch28's 반증 조건 1 requires three papers with absolute units and three or more points on the axis; 반증 조건 8 requires three papers satisfying R1·R3·R4. This paper satisfies R4 alone. Verdict 1 stands.

verdict_6.detail: ch28 판정 6 attributes the $B_s$ silence to inherited reporting convention rather than measurement difficulty. This paper is the strongest available evidence for that diagnosis: a team whose entire contribution is a 'unified budget view' (§3, p.3), who formalise every method by what it spends and what feedback it observes, still chose rollouts as the unit and printed no compute quantity anywhere. Nobody had more reason to count tokens, and nobody counted.

verdict_5.relation: QUALIFIES — this is the one place the paper pushes back
verdict_5.detail: ch28 판정 5 records that R1–R9 are cheap: '아홉 중 새 실험을 요구하는 것은 R3 하나뿐이고... 나머지 여덟은 전부 이미 존재하는 실행 로그의 인쇄다' [ch28 §28.3.7]. The cheapness claim is not refuted — this team's logs certainly contain their token counts. What is refuted is the implicit inference that cheapness will produce compliance. The most methodologically self-conscious paper in view, whose stated contribution is a matched-budget protocol, did not print them. ch28 §28.3.7's closing [평가] should absorb this: the cost has been low since the founding paper and the cell is still empty, so the missing ingredient is a reporting norm, not a budget.

new_taxonomy_form.detail: ch28's six bins have no cell for this paper's reporting form. $K=5$ rollouts with $m=1$ per task is not (a) absolute FLOPs or tokens, not (b) optimizer steps, not (c) wall-clock, and it is more concrete than (d) an ungraduated ordinal, because a rollout is a countable unit of work with a stated protocol — yet it is not a compute unit, since Table 4 bounds one rollout at 300 turns x 128,000 generated tokens. This is a seventh form: a COUNT OF AGENT ROLLOUTS OR INTERACTIONS. ch28 §28.2.1's taxonomy_gaps list (PLOS simulation time, EWC sample count, Generative Adapter figure-only, PAD absent) gains a fifth entry, and this one is likely to become the dominant form as the $E$-path moves into agent territory. A monograph that wants its census to age well should add the bin now.

new_regime_for_the_axis.relation: ADDS a data point ch28 §28.3.1 predicts
new_regime_for_the_axis.detail: ch28 표 28-4 argues that $B_s$ differs from $(N,D)$ because its denominator $N_q$ is finite and workload-dependent. This paper supplies the corpus's most favourable $N_q$ — one artifact amortised over an entire task distribution, 34 held-out tasks in §4.4 — and the method still fails. That is a boundary result for the accounting: when the amortisation denominator is made as large as the design allows and the artifact is a shared prefix, the cost side of the argument is maximally favourable and the method still loses, because the binding constraint is transfer, not cost. ch28 §28.3.5's 'so what can still be said' section can use this: the $E$-path's failure mode here is on the QUALITY axis at a point where the COST axis was handed every advantage.

verdict_2.relation: CONFIRMS, with an independent fifth system and a new content type
verdict_2.quote: ch27 판정 2 — '$E$-경로는 유망하다. 단 비용 방법으로서다. 품질 방법으로서는 현재 문헌이 지지하지 않으며, 그 반증은 이 책이 아니라 논문들 자신의 표에서 나온다.'
verdict_2.detail: The quality winner in this paper is a memory-free, scaffold-free configuration: Parallel Sampling on an initial harness explicitly defined as 'a single bash tool and nothing else, without skills, middleware, or persistent memory' [App. A.1, p.11], scoring the best average in Table 1 (72.3) and the best pass@1 average in Table 2 (86.0). The pattern ch27 records for Mem0, Zep and ReasoningBank recurs in a benchmark, a system family and a research community that share nothing with them. And the new content type widens the evidence base rather than duplicating it: this $E$ is procedural, its scope is per-deployment rather than per-user, and its write is verified by a real unit test rather than an LLM judge — the strongest write hygiene in the corpus — and it still does not transfer.

verdict_5.relation: CONFIRMS the pattern, with the missing control on the other side
verdict_5.quote: ch27 §27.3.5의 [평가]: '실행된 대조에서는 방법이 지거나 겨우 비기고, 방법이 이기는 축에서는 대조가 실행되지 않았다... 빠진 것은 언제나 가장 싸고 가장 자명한 baseline이다.'
verdict_5.detail: A textbook new instance, and it runs in the opposite direction, which makes the pattern more general than ch27 stated it. Here the omitted control protects the CRITIC, not the method: §4.4 is the setting where a reusable artifact could show a genuine transferable gain, and it is the setting where the competing arms are declared inapplicable. ch27's formulation should be widened from 'the method's authors omit the hard baseline' to 'whichever side would be decided by the missing arm, that arm is the one that is missing'. The evidence table 표 27-4 gains a row that belongs to a critique paper rather than a method paper.

verdict_4_theta_condition_iii.detail: ch27 판정 4 lists as $\Theta$-path condition (iii) 'a procedure that judges writes without labels, and its accuracy measured'. This paper runs the labelled version of that procedure on the $E$-path — the write is selected by an executed unit test [§3.4, p.4] — and the artifact still fails to transfer [Table 3, p.7]. Write verification and write generality are therefore separable, and passing the former does not deliver the latter. Any chapter that treats verification as the bottleneck should carry this.

ch15_and_reasoningbank.relation: CONFIRMS, twice, from an independent source
ch15_and_reasoningbank.detail_1: The dossier's ReasoningBank caveat — monotone degradation as retrieved experience grows (49.7 → 46.0 → 45.5 → 44.4) — gains an independent mechanism statement from a different lab, a different benchmark and a different artifact type: 'the growing volume of persistent prompt text introduces context bloat that can offset the remaining gains' [§5.1, p.8]. Two observations of the same sign with no citation link between them.
ch15_and_reasoningbank.detail_2: The dossier's other ReasoningBank caveat — a 72.7%-accurate judge — gets its limiting case. Here the judge is the agent itself, with no external correctness signal, and five rounds of self-judged (U-E) writes push a strong model DOWN by 5.6 points (GPT-5.4: 75.3 → 69.7) [Table 1, p.6]. The paper's own conclusion is the one the monograph should quote: 'harness revision likely requires a reliable external correctness signal to ground the revision process' [§4.2, p.6]. This is also the corpus's cleanest sign observation for $\rho$ under self-generated feedback, even though the rate itself is unreported.

ch11_and_ch24.relation: CONFIRMS condition (1) with an independent second justification; MILDLY THREATENS the per-paper census format
ch11_and_ch24.quote: ch11 §11.2.3: '(1)을 빼면 — 모든 쓰기가 sleep이 된다... 조건 (1)이 없으면 이 둘의 쓰기와 sleep 라운드의 쓰기가 구분되지 않고... 그러면 sleep-time compute은 그냥 쓰기의 다른 이름이 된다.'
ch11_and_ch24.confirmation: The monograph justified condition (1) mechanistically. This paper justifies the same cut evidentially and independently — when the write has seen the evaluation task, the measured gain cannot be attributed to the artifact — and it builds an entire experimental protocol around the point. Two unrelated derivations selecting the same condition is the best corroboration a definitional choice can get.
ch11_and_ch24.new_foil: Harness Scaling is the sharpest illustration of condition (1) available anywhere: the same write operator, the same store, the same budget magnitude, the same meta agent, differing from Harness Evolution only in whether the update is conditioned on the evaluation task. ch11 §11.2.3's exposition of condition (1) currently leans on MemGPT and SCM, both of which differ from sleep writes in several respects at once. This one differs in exactly one.
ch11_and_ch24.threat: The census format assigns one verdict per paper (통과 9 / 경계 1 / 불충족 19 over 29). This paper cannot be so assigned: Harness Evolution passes under one of its own protocols and fails under another with the mechanism held identical, and the paper additionally contains an explicit non-candidate foil. ch27's B4 already recorded setting-dependent passage for `Do LMs Need Sleep?`, so the phenomenon is not new — but this is the sharper instance, and as the $E$-path moves into agent evaluation such papers will become common. ch24 §24.3 should state explicitly that the discriminant applies to (mechanism, protocol) pairs. This is a limitation of the presentation, not an error in any count.

ch25.relation: CONFIRMS the structural finding; ADDS a boundary regime; changes no count
ch25.detail: All four cost cells are empty again, and since the paper is outside the 29-paper corpus no census count moves. What it adds is a regime ch25's typology does not contain: an $E$-path artifact amortised over a task distribution rather than a context. ch25 판정 2's structural defect — the per-query prompt term does not divide by $N_q$ — applies here in its mildest possible form, since $N_q=34$ and the artifact is a shared prefix across the whole deployment. The method still fails. **The accounting can be handed every advantage and the method can still lose, because ch25 measures cost and this failure is in transfer.** That is a useful boundary statement for ch25 §25.5: a favourable $L^\ast$ or $N_q^\ast$ is necessary, not sufficient, and no cost accounting can rescue an artifact that carries nothing generalisable.

ch26.relation: ADDS a capacity shape; confirms the zero count
ch26.detail: ch26's map has per-session $W$ (transient, hot), per-user $\Theta$ delta (persistent, warm) and per-user or per-session $E$ (persistent, cold). This paper supplies a fourth shape: a PER-DEPLOYMENT $E$ whose bytes are O(1) in users — one harness serving the whole task distribution. It is the only state shape in view that does not grow with users, and therefore the cheapest capacity profile any path can offer. It is also, of course, unsized: no byte, character or token count for the artifact appears anywhere, so ch26's count of papers printing $C_{\text{cap}}$ is unchanged. The shape is worth a row in ch26 §26.2's table because it bounds what the $E$-path's best case looks like.

ch30.relation: REINFORCES one row; supplies one new, cheap, high-value falsifier
ch30.reinforced: ch30's row '$E$-경로에서 품질 1위가 반복적으로 기억 시스템 없는 구성이다' gains its fifth instance, with a falsifying observation still unmet.
ch30.new_falsifier: The single most valuable missing experiment the monograph can now name concretely: **run this paper's §4.4 held-out protocol WITH the Parallel Sampling and Sequential Refinement arms at matched $K$, and report tokens.** That is one table. It would simultaneously satisfy R1, R3 (if $K$ is swept), R4 and R6, and it would answer, for a discriminant-passing $E$-path procedure, the question ch27 판정 5 left as 판정 불가 and ch28 판정 1 left as ungraphable. Nobody has printed it. Because the enabling infrastructure now demonstrably exists — this paper built all four arms and the held-out split — the falsifier's cost is close to zero, which is exactly the criterion ch30 uses to rank its list.

book_impact.chapters_with_no_impact: ch01–ch10 (Part I concepts), ch12, ch16–ch23 ($W$- and $\Theta$-path chapters, plus biology and capacity theory) take nothing from this paper. It contains no weight update, no fast-weight state, no gradient, no biological argument and no capacity theory, and its bibliography touches none of those literatures. ch29 takes nothing directly either, though its sandbox-provisioning observation (App. A.4, p.11) is a cost class the four-cell frame cannot hold and may be worth one sentence there.
